hero.headline: Death toll reaches 8 in Longview paper mill disaster
hero.body:
The death toll from a chemical tank rupture at a paper mill in Longview, Washington, has risen to eight after recovery crews found the remains of six missing workers, authorities confirmed on Thursday.

Nine workers were initially reported missing following the incident at the Nippon Dynawave Packaging facility. Three individuals remain unaccounted for and are presumed dead. Eight other people sustained injuries in the disaster, including a firefighter who responded to the scene.

The tank contained approximately 600,000 gallons of white liquor, a chemical mixture made primarily of sodium hydroxide and sodium sulfide. The substance is used in the paper industry to break down wood and produce kraft paper, which is commonly used for packaging, shopping bags, and other products. About 25,000 gallons of the liquid remained in the damaged tank and continued to leak slowly.

When the tank ruptured, white liquor spilled into a drainage ditch and contaminated the surrounding area. Officials confirmed that contamination had reached the Columbia River by Tuesday, and dead carp were discovered in the water. State ecology department officials urged the public to avoid ditches and dikes in the area while water testing continued. However, authorities said there were no issues related to air quality or drinking water in the city of Longview.

Recovery operations began Wednesday following a delay caused by concerns about the structural integrity of the damaged tank. Officials stated there was no hope of finding additional survivors and transitioned the operation from rescue to recovery. Matt Amos with the Longview fire department said the effort would be "slow, methodical and deliberate," with recovered victims undergoing decontamination before being transported to the coroner's office. Responders worked in chemical protective equipment while prioritizing safety.

Washington Governor Bob Ferguson said at a Wednesday news conference that authorities were "bracing ourselves for this being the deadliest industrial tragedy in modern Washington state history."

The U.S. Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board announced it was launching a federal investigation into the incident. The Washington state department of ecology and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency were overseeing operations to assess environmental impacts.

Brian Wood, representing Nippon Dynawave, a subsidiary of Japan-based Nippon Paper Group, said the company was focused on supporting victims and first responders. He pledged that the company would "cooperate to the maximum extent" with investigators.

Prior to the disaster, safety complaints had been filed against the facility in March and May. The state's labor and industries department said both complaints were unrelated to the current situation. Since 2021, the company had been fined $3,400 for three separate health and safety violations discovered by state inspectors.

The sprawling Longview plant employs approximately 1,000 people and produces material for tissues, printing paper, cups, plates, and cartons.

cards.headline: U.S. Officials Say Framework Reached to Extend Iran Cease-Fire
cards.teaser: An emerging agreement could extend the cease-fire and enable broader negotiations, though President Trump has not yet approved the framework.
cards.body:
U.S. officials say they are working toward an arrangement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and extend the current cease-fire with Iran. Vice President Vance stated the two countries are close to a deal but have not yet reached one. President Trump has not approved the emerging framework.

The potential agreement could allow for an extended cease-fire and pave the way for more substantive negotiations between the U.S. and Iran. However, the framework still requires approval from both Trump and Iranian leadership before it can take effect.

cards.headline: US and Iran near agreement to extend ceasefire, reopen Strait of Hormuz
cards.body:
The United States and Iran have reached a tentative agreement to extend their ceasefire by 60 days, reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and establish a framework for talks on Tehran's nuclear program, according to US officials. Vice President JD Vance said on Thursday that the two countries were "very close" to finalizing a memorandum of understanding, though some sticking points remained.

"We're very close but not there yet," Vance said, adding that the US was still "going back and forth" with Iran on nuclear issues.

Negotiators have been working to finalize the terms of the agreement. US officials told the BBC that the framework of a ceasefire extension deal had been agreed, pending approval from President Trump and Iran's leadership. A second round of negotiations would "very likely" be held in Islamabad, according to White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt.

The tentative deal comes after weeks of indirect negotiations, with Pakistan playing a key role in mediation efforts. Pakistan's army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, led a delegation to Tehran on Wednesday to convey messages from Washington. Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also launched a four-day regional tour to Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Turkey to coordinate support for peace efforts.

Leavitt said the White House remained "very much engaged" in negotiations and felt "good about the prospects of a deal." However, she emphasized that nothing was official until announced by the White House.

The proposed agreement would extend the ceasefire beyond its expiration on April 22 and launch further diplomatic efforts. The memorandum would create a framework for broader talks on Tehran's nuclear program and address concerns about Iran's nuclear capabilities. The Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global oil shipments, would reopen under the terms being discussed.

News of the potential breakthrough led to falling oil prices on Thursday, reflecting market optimism about the deal.

However, complications remain on the ground. Sources in Tehran indicated that Iran demanded an end to Israeli attacks on Lebanon as a precondition for another round of negotiations with the US. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu signaled that Israel was continuing military operations against Hezbollah in Lebanon, indicating a potential obstacle to broader regional peace.

The US military has also imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports following earlier negotiations. US warships turned back nine ships, including a Chinese-owned tanker, attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday.

Trump and his advisers have previously believed they were close to a deal several times during negotiations, only to see talks stall. The signing of the memorandum of understanding would represent the most significant diplomatic breakthrough since the war began.

cards.headline: U.S. and Iran near tentative ceasefire extension and nuclear talks agreement
cards.teaser: American and Iranian negotiators reached a tentative 60-day agreement pending approval from President Trump and Iranian leadership.
cards.body:
U.S. and Iran officials say they are close to a tentative 60-day ceasefire extension agreement that would also reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Vice President Vance stated the two countries are "very close" to a deal but "not there yet," with ongoing negotiations focused on nuclear issues.

The framework for the ceasefire extension has been agreed upon in principle, though the deal requires final approval from President Trump and Iran's leadership before taking effect. Recent U.S. strikes on Iran have occurred even as peace talks continue.

cards.headline: Netanyahu orders Israeli forces to expand Gaza control to 70%
cards.teaser: The Israeli prime minister directed the military to increase territorial control in Gaza, contradicting ceasefire terms.
cards.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has directed the Israel Defense Forces to increase their control of Gaza to 70 percent of the territory. This expansion would represent a significant increase in the area under Israeli military authority.

The directive conflicts with the ceasefire agreement that Israel and Hamas reached in October 2025, which established specific territorial arrangements that the new orders would breach.

cards.headline: Supreme Court sides with Mississippi death row inmate in racial bias case
cards.teaser: The court ruled in favor of a Mississippi man on death row who alleged racial bias in his conviction.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court issued a decision supporting a Mississippi death row inmate in a case involving allegations of racial bias during jury selection. The ruling in the case addresses constitutional protections related to jury composition and racial discrimination in capital trials.

Justice Brett Kavanaugh authored the opinion, which legal observers described as a victory for racial justice in the criminal justice system. The decision reinforces legal protections against race-based exclusion of jurors in death penalty cases.

cards.headline: Blue Origin rocket explodes on Florida launch pad
cards.teaser: A New Glenn rocket operated by Blue Origin exploded during a test at Cape Canaveral.
cards.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded on a launch pad at Cape Canaveral in Florida on Thursday night during a test. Blue Origin, founded by Jeff Bezos, described the incident as an "anomaly" in a social media statement.

The company confirmed that all personnel were accounted for and no one was harmed. Blue Origin said it would provide updates as more information became available about what caused the explosion.

hero.headline: Russian Drone Strikes Apartment Building in Romania
hero.body:
A Russian drone struck an apartment building in the Romanian city of Galati, injuring two people, according to Romania's defense ministry. The incident occurred near the country's border with Ukraine.

Romania is a member of NATO. The strike on its territory represents a direct impact of the ongoing conflict between Russia and Ukraine on a NATO member state.

Galati is located in eastern Romania, close to the Ukrainian border. The city has been in proximity to the war zone since Russia's invasion of Ukraine began.

The Romanian defense ministry confirmed that a Russian drone was responsible for the attack. Two people sustained injuries in the strike on the residential building.

The incident comes as Russian forces continue military operations in Ukraine. Drones have been a regular feature of the conflict, used by both sides for reconnaissance and attacks.

NATO's collective defense principle, enshrined in Article 5 of the alliance's founding treaty, states that an attack on one member is considered an attack on all members. However, the alliance has not indicated how it will respond to this incident.

Romanian authorities are assessing the damage and the circumstances of the strike. The country has been a supporter of Ukraine since the invasion began, providing humanitarian aid and serving as a transit point for refugees.

The strike represents an escalation in terms of geographic impact, with the conflict now directly affecting infrastructure and civilians in a NATO member country. Previous incidents have seen stray munitions land in border areas, but direct strikes on residential buildings are less common.

Romania shares a border with Ukraine and has been monitoring the security situation closely since the war began. The country has also hosted Ukrainian refugees and provided support to its neighbor.

cards.headline: U.S. Officials Say Framework Reached to Extend Iran Cease-Fire
cards.teaser: An emerging agreement could extend the cease-fire and enable broader negotiations, though President Trump has not yet approved the framework.
cards.body:

cards.headline: U.S. Military Accuses Iran of Cease-Fire Violation After Kuwait Missile Attack
cards.teaser: The U.S. Central Command says Iran launched missiles at Kuwait, testing the fragile truce between the two countries.
cards.body:
The U.S. military said Iran violated a cease-fire agreement after Kuwait experienced a missile attack. U.S. Central Command characterized the incident as a serious breach of the truce.

The strike occurred amid reports of a tentative deal to extend the cease-fire between the two countries. U.S. officials indicated they were working toward arrangements to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which could support extending the cease-fire and enable broader negotiations. President Trump has not yet approved the emerging framework.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Designates Brazilian Drug Gangs as Terrorist Groups
cards.teaser: The U.S. has labeled Brazil's two largest drug gangs as terrorist organizations after warnings from the administration.
cards.body:
The Trump administration has designated Brazil's two largest drug gangs as terrorist groups. The action follows through on earlier threats made by the administration.

The designation came after a new push by members of the Bolsonaro family. The move allows the U.S. to impose additional sanctions and legal measures against the organizations and their members. The two gangs are among the most powerful criminal organizations operating in Brazil.

cards.headline: Israel Cuts Ties With U.N. Chief After Sexual Violence Blacklist Inclusion
cards.teaser: Israel severed relations with the U.N. secretary general after being added to a blacklist for conflict-related sexual violence.
cards.body:
Israel announced it would cut ties with the United Nations secretary general after the organization included the country on its blacklist for sexual violence in conflict zones. Russia was also added to the newly updated list, which identifies parties credibly suspected of committing or being responsible for patterns of sexual violence in armed conflict.

Israel objected to being placed on the same blacklist as Hamas and other parties accused of sexual violence during armed conflicts.

cards.headline: Portugal Records Hottest May Day as Europe Faces Heat Wave
cards.teaser: Portugal broke its record for the hottest day in May as a heat wave sweeps across Europe.
cards.body:
Portugal set a new record for the hottest May day as a heat wave affects multiple European countries. French students are taking exams in sweltering schools, and Italy has issued red alerts.

The extreme temperatures represent part of a broader heat wave moving across the continent. Authorities in affected countries have issued warnings and advisories as temperatures climb to unusual levels for late May. The heat wave has prompted concerns about public health and safety across the region.

cards.headline: Over 1.5 Million Pilgrims Begin Hajj Amid Regional Tensions
cards.teaser: Muslim pilgrims are performing Hajj rituals as Eid al-Adha celebrations start, with thousands of Iranians traveling to Saudi Arabia during wartime.
cards.body:
More than 1.5 million pilgrims have begun the annual Hajj pilgrimage to Mecca amid regional tensions. Muslim pilgrims are performing rituals under intense heat as Eid al-Adha celebrations commence.

Thousands of Iranians traveled to Saudi Arabia for the pilgrimage despite the ongoing conflict involving Iran. A report finds that global heating is making the Hajj increasingly dangerous for participants. The journey represents a significant religious obligation for Muslims, drawing pilgrims from around the world to Saudi Arabia.

cards.headline: U.S. military strike kills 2 in eastern Pacific
cards.teaser: Two people died after a U.S. military strike on a suspected narco boat in the eastern Pacific Ocean.
cards.body:
The U.S. military conducted a strike on a boat suspected of drug trafficking in the eastern Pacific, killing two men. The attack targeted what officials described as an alleged drug vessel operating in international waters.

Survivors from the strike were left at sea following the attack. The overall death toll from recent U.S. boat strikes in the region has reached 199 people, according to reports tracking military operations against suspected drug smuggling vessels.

cards.teaser: American and Iranian negotiators reached a tentative 60-day agreement pending approval from President Trump and Iranian leadership.

U.S. and Iran officials say they are close to a tentative 60-day ceasefire extension agreement that would also reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Vice President Vance stated the two countries are "very close" to a deal but "not there yet," with ongoing negotiations focused on nuclear issues.

cards.teaser: A New Glenn rocket operated by Blue Origin exploded during a test at Cape Canaveral.
cards.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded on a launch pad at Cape Canaveral in Florida on Thursday night during a test. Blue Origin, founded by Jeff Bezos, described the incident as an "anomaly" in a social media statement.

The company confirmed that all personnel were accounted for and no one was harmed. Blue Origin said it would provide updates as more information became available about what caused the explosion.

cards.headline: Supreme Court sides with Mississippi death row inmate in racial bias case
cards.teaser: The court ruled in favor of a Mississippi man on death row who alleged racial bias in his conviction.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court issued a decision supporting a Mississippi death row inmate in a case involving allegations of racial bias during jury selection. The ruling in the case addresses constitutional protections related to jury composition and racial discrimination in capital trials.

Justice Brett Kavanaugh authored the opinion, which legal observers described as a victory for racial justice in the criminal justice system. The decision reinforces legal protections against race-based exclusion of jurors in death penalty cases.

cards.headline: Michigan Governor Whitmer reverses position on 2028 presidential run
cards.teaser: Governor Gretchen Whitmer initially said she would not run for president in 2028, then walked back her statement hours later.
cards.body:
Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer announced she would not run for president in 2028, appearing to end speculation about a potential White House bid. However, she quickly reversed the statement, walking back her declaration.

Whitmer had been considered a top Democratic candidate for the 2028 presidential race. Her initial announcement seemed to remove her from consideration, but the rapid reversal left her political intentions uncertain.

cards.headline: Judge allows Trump mail-in voting restrictions to stand temporarily
cards.teaser: A federal judge declined to immediately block an executive order limiting mail-in voting access.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Washington, D.C., has declined to temporarily block President Trump's executive order that restricts mail-in voting. Democrats had sought an emergency injunction to prevent the order from taking effect while legal challenges proceed.

The judge's decision allows the voting restrictions to move forward for now. Another judge may rule on the order soon as additional legal challenges continue.

hero.headline: Dell shares surge 39% on AI-driven earnings beat
hero.teaser: The computer maker reported its fastest sales growth since returning to public markets in 2018.
hero.body:
Dell Technologies shares jumped 39% after the company lifted its forecasts and reported earnings that exceeded analyst estimates. The surge was driven by strong demand for servers and infrastructure used in AI data center construction.

The company reported its fastest sales growth since it returned to public markets in 2018. Dell's stock reached toward another record high as investors rewarded the earnings beat, which the company attributed directly to the ongoing AI boom fueling demand for data center equipment.

cards.headline: Fertitta Entertainment acquires Caesars in $17.6 billion deal
cards.teaser: The sale of the Las Vegas Strip icon gives Tilman Fertitta control of four Atlantic City casinos.
cards.body:
Caesars Entertainment has been sold to Fertitta Entertainment for $17.6 billion, or nearly $6 billion in one reported valuation. The acquisition makes Tilman Fertitta one of the dominant players on the Las Vegas Strip and gives his company control of four Atlantic City casinos.

The deal represents a major consolidation in the casino industry. Caesars has been an icon on the Las Vegas Strip for decades. Fertitta Entertainment already operates Golden Nugget properties, and the Caesars acquisition significantly expands its footprint in key gaming markets.

cards.headline: Stock markets reach new highs on US-Iran deal and corporate earnings
cards.teaser: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq rose as oil prices pulled back on reports of a diplomatic breakthrough.
cards.body:
Wall Street reached new highs as investors responded positively to corporate earnings and progress in US-Iran negotiations. According to US officials, the framework for a ceasefire extension deal has been agreed, though it still requires approval from Trump and Iran's leadership. Oil prices declined on the news of the potential diplomatic breakthrough.

The market gains reflected optimism that a Middle East deal could ease regional tensions. Strong earnings reports, including a surge in Dell's stock, contributed to the rally across major indices including the S&P 500 and Nasdaq.

cards.headline: ABC files station license renewals under protest, accuses FCC of retaliation
cards.teaser: The network says the commission moved up expiration dates in an unconstitutional campaign.
cards.body:
ABC has accused the Trump administration's Federal Communications Commission of targeting its broadcast licenses in what the network characterizes as unconstitutional retaliation. The company filed station license renewal applications under protest while challenging the regulatory action.

FCC Chairman Brendan Carr moved up the expiration date of ABC's station licenses to May 28, prompting the network to submit early renewal filings. ABC maintains that the FCC's actions violate constitutional protections and has called for the agency to reverse course on what it views as a targeted campaign against the broadcaster.

cards.headline: Federal regulators pause Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern rail merger review
cards.teaser: The Surface Transportation Board accepted a revised merger application but delayed proceedings.
cards.body:
The Surface Transportation Board paused review of the proposed $71.5 billion merger between Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern. The board accepted a revised merger application from the two railroads but announced it would delay further proceedings.

Union Pacific refuted new claims from state attorneys general, saying it had provided all requested answers in its merger paperwork. The companies have promoted the deal as creating America's first transcontinental railroad, but the merger hit regulatory obstacles as federal officials sought additional information.

cards.headline: Treasury launches Trump Accounts app for $1,000 newborn investment program
cards.teaser: The app allows families to manage federal investments given to children born in the US.
cards.body:
The US Treasury rolled out the Trump Accounts app nationwide, allowing parents to track and manage $1,000 federal investments given to newborns. Treasury Secretary Bessent announced the app would go live, making the program accessible to families across the country.

The accounts provide each child born in the United States with a $1,000 federal investment. The app launched to enable parents to monitor these investments and manage the accounts as the program expands nationwide.

cards.headline: Treasury prepares legislation to put Trump on new $250 bill
cards.teaser: The plan would require Congress to allow a living person to appear on US
cards.body:
The White House is pushing Congress to approve a $250 bill featuring Donald Trump's portrait, according to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. The proposal would celebrate the United States' 250th anniversary of independence.

Current federal law prohibits printing images of living people on US currency. Trump allies in Congress are working to change this law to allow the exception. The Treasury Department has already begun preparations for the potential new currency. Democrats have vowed to block the move.

hero.headline: James Webb Space Telescope finds black hole that formed before its galaxy
hero.teaser: NASA's telescope discovered a supermassive black hole that appears to have formed before the galaxy surrounding it.
hero.body:
The James Webb Space Telescope identified a supermassive black hole in the early universe that formed before its host galaxy, upending conventional understanding of how galaxies and black holes develop. Scientists previously believed galaxies formed first, with black holes developing at their centers afterward.

The discovery was described as a paradigm shift in astrophysics. The black hole, referred to as a 'little red dot' in early universe observations, exists without the typical surrounding galaxy structure. Researchers are working to understand how such a formation sequence could occur.

cards.headline: Waymo leads autonomous vehicle registrations in Texas as Tesla lags
cards.teaser: New tracking data shows Waymo operating significantly more registered autonomous vehicles than Tesla in Texas.
cards.body:
A new Texas law and tracking tool provide detailed accounting of autonomous vehicle registrations in the state, revealing Waymo's dominance in the robotaxi and self-driving truck sector. The data shows Tesla trailing behind in registered autonomous vehicles despite its public focus on self-driving technology.

The tracking system offers the clearest view yet of how many autonomous vehicles different companies are operating in Texas. The state has become a testing ground for self-driving technology as companies seek to expand their robotaxi and autonomous freight operations.

cards.headline: AI startup Glean reaches $300 million in annual revenue
cards.teaser: The enterprise AI search company tripled its revenue despite competition from major tech companies.
cards.body:
Glean, an enterprise AI search startup, surpassed $300 million in annual revenue, tripling its sales even as large tech companies entered the same market. The company has positioned AI-driven budget reduction as its primary value proposition to corporate customers.

The revenue growth comes at a time when tech giants have launched competing AI search products for enterprise use. Glean has differentiated itself by focusing on cost savings and efficiency gains for businesses adopting AI tools.

cards.headline: Cloud providers redesign infrastructure for AI agent traffic
cards.teaser: Amazon Web Services, Cloudflare, and other companies are rebuilding internet infrastructure to handle machine-generated traffic.
cards.body:
Major cloud infrastructure providers including AWS and Cloudflare are redesigning their systems to accommodate AI agents moving from experimental use to production deployment. The companies are preparing for a shift away from human-generated internet traffic toward machine-to-machine communication.

The infrastructure changes reflect expectations that AI agents will become a dominant source of internet activity. Cloud providers are adapting their networks, security systems, and data handling capabilities to serve automated systems rather than primarily human users.

cards.headline: Large language models accept false information even when warned
cards.teaser: Testing shows AI language models display bias toward representing false statements as true despite explicit warnings.
cards.body:
Research has found that large language models confidently present false statements as true, even after being explicitly warned that the information is incorrect. Fine-tuning tests revealed a persistent bias in these systems toward representing claims as accurate regardless of accuracy warnings provided to them.

This discovery raises significant concerns about the reliability of AI systems in applications where factual accuracy is essential. The pattern was observed across multiple language models during controlled testing.

cards.headline: Developer adds data deletion code to library targeting AI coding tools
cards.teaser: A programmer inserted a prompt injection into open-source code that instructed AI agents to delete application output.
cards.body:
A software developer frustrated with AI-assisted coding added an undisclosed prompt injection to the jqwik code library that instructed AI coding agents to delete application output. The addition was described as a response to what the developer called 'vibe coders' who rely heavily on AI tools.

The prompt injection was embedded in a way that would be executed by AI coding assistants reading the library's code. The incident highlights tensions between traditional developers and those using AI-powered coding tools.

cards.headline: Slate Auto to announce electric vehicle pricing in June
cards.teaser: The Bezos-backed startup will take preorders for its EV on June 24 ahead of planned year-end deliveries.
cards.body:
Slate Auto will reveal pricing for its electric vehicle and open preorders on June 24. The Bezos-backed startup is preparing to launch its first vehicle to market.

The company aims to begin shipping vehicles by the end of this year.

hero.headline: Claude Lemieux, four-time Stanley Cup champion, dies at 60
hero.body:
Claude Lemieux, a four-time Stanley Cup winner whose aggressive playing style made him both feared and respected throughout the NHL, has died at age 60. Authorities confirmed Thursday that Lemieux died by suicide.

The Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office responded to a call at a furniture store showroom in Lake Park, Florida, just after 3 a.m. Thursday morning. The sheriff's office identified the victim as Lemieux.

Lemieux built a memorable career as a fierce competitor known for his hard-hitting approach to the game. He won Stanley Cup championships with three different teams: the Montreal Canadiens, the New Jersey Devils twice, and the Colorado Avalanche. His physical style of play sometimes drew criticism from opponents, but his ability to perform in crucial moments earned him respect throughout the league.

The winger's most celebrated achievement came in 1995 when he won the Conn Smythe Trophy as playoff MVP while helping the New Jersey Devils capture their first Stanley Cup championship. Over his NHL career spanning from 1983 to 2003, Lemieux played 21 seasons and recorded 379 goals and 406 assists across 1,215 regular season games. In the postseason, he added 80 goals and 78 assists in 234 playoff appearances, establishing himself as one of hockey's premier playoff performers.

Lemieux's intensity on the ice was legendary. His fiery demeanor and willingness to engage in physical confrontations made him a polarizing figure throughout his playing days. Yet this same competitive fire translated into clutch performances when stakes were highest, particularly during playoff runs with his championship teams.

After retiring as a player, Lemieux transitioned into work as a player agent, continuing his involvement in professional hockey. His son Brendan Lemieux has gone on to play in the NHL, continuing the family's hockey legacy.

Throughout his career, Lemieux played for eight NHL franchises, including stints with the Coyotes, Stars, and Sharks in addition to his championship teams. This nomadic journey reflected both his value as a veteran presence and the way the league valued his playoff experience and ability to contribute to championship efforts.

The hockey community expressed heartfelt condolences following news of his death. Lemieux's passing adds to recent losses within professional sports and reminds the hockey world of the legacy he left across multiple franchises during championship runs spanning the 1980s through early 2000s.

His death also highlights the importance of mental health awareness and support systems for former athletes, as the sports community continues to grapple with the challenges faced by those who have left the spotlight after successful careers.

cards.headline: Kyle Busch died from pneumonia complications, death certificate shows
cards.teaser: The former NASCAR star's death certificate shows he suffered from bacterial pneumonia for weeks before his death last week.
cards.body:
Kyle Busch died from hemorrhagic shock and disseminated intravascular coagulation following complications from bacterial pneumonia that had affected him for weeks. These conditions developed after the pneumonia progressed to sepsis.

According to his death certificate, the former NASCAR star's condition deteriorated as the bacterial infection spread throughout his body, triggering a cascade of life-threatening complications that ultimately led to his death.

cards.headline: MLB owners propose hard salary cap in contract negotiations
cards.teaser: Major League Baseball owners made their first firm salary cap proposal since the 1994 strike that canceled the World Series.
cards.body:
Major League Baseball owners proposed a hard salary cap to players Thursday as part of negotiations for the next collective bargaining agreement. This marks the first firm cap proposal from owners since 1994.

The 1994 salary cap proposal triggered a players strike that led to the cancellation of that year's World Series. The current collective bargaining agreement between MLB and the players union is set to expire, prompting the new round of negotiations between the two sides.

cards.headline: NBA changes draft lottery system to discourage tanking
cards.teaser: The league's Board of Governors approved a new lottery format aimed at preventing teams from intentionally losing games.
cards.body:
The NBA Board of Governors voted to approve a new draft lottery system designed to address tanking. The league expanded the lottery and implemented changes to discourage teams from deliberately losing games to improve their draft position.

Under the new system, the Memphis Grizzlies will not be able to receive a top-five pick from the Utah Jazz due to the revised lottery rules. The NBA explained the specific mechanisms that prevent certain draft pick transfers under the updated format.

cards.headline: Knicks center Mitchell Robinson breaks finger before NBA Finals
cards.teaser: The New York center suffered a broken right pinkie finger with no timetable for return.
cards.body:
Knicks center Mitchell Robinson has suffered a broken right pinkie finger ahead of the NBA Finals, according to ESPN's Shams Charania. There is no timetable for his return.

The injury comes as the Knicks prepare for the championship series after snapping their 27-year NBA Finals drought with an 11-game playoff winning streak.

cards.headline: Alabama beats UCLA in Women's College World Series opener
cards.teaser: Top-seeded Alabama rallied behind Megan Grant's NCAA-record 41st home run of the season.
cards.body:
Top-seeded Alabama rallied past UCLA in Thursday's opening round of the Women's College World Series. Megan Grant powered the victory with her 41st home run of the season, breaking the NCAA record for homers in a single season.

The historic blast proved crucial as Alabama advanced through the double-elimination tournament with the win.

cards.headline: Puka Nacua thanks Rams for support after civil lawsuit
cards.teaser: The wide receiver expressed gratitude to the organization following a lawsuit filed against him in March.
cards.body:
Puka Nacua expressed gratitude toward the Rams organization for its support following a civil lawsuit filed against him in March. The wide receiver publicly acknowledged the team's backing during the legal proceedings.

The Rams have stood by Nacua as the case moves through the court system.

hero.headline: Bari Weiss fires multiple staff members in 60 Minutes overhaul
hero.body:
Bari Weiss has begun restructuring CBS's 60 Minutes with several staff firings as part of a major leadership change at the long-running news program.

Weiss named Nick Bilton to lead the show as its new executive producer. The appointments mark a significant shift in direction for the CBS News flagship program.

Correspondent Cecilia Vega was fired from 60 Minutes and released a memo criticizing CBS News following her dismissal. Longtime correspondent Sharyn Alfonsi also departed the program as part of the changes.

The shake-up represents one of the most substantial personnel changes in recent memory for 60 Minutes, which has maintained a relatively stable roster of correspondents and producers for years. The program has been a cornerstone of CBS News programming since its debut in 1968.

Weiss, a former New York Times opinion editor and founder of The Free Press, took on the role of overseeing changes at the news magazine. Her appointment to a position of influence at CBS News had generated attention in media circles prior to the announced personnel moves.

Bilton, the newly appointed executive producer, brings experience from various media organizations to the role. His selection signals a potential shift in editorial approach for the program.

Vega's memo following her firing suggests tension surrounding the departures. She had joined 60 Minutes as a correspondent and her exit removes one of the program's on-air personalities. The specific contents of her criticism of CBS News were reported but not detailed in available sources.

Alfonsi's expected departure removes another veteran presence from the correspondent lineup. She had been with 60 Minutes for multiple years, covering a range of investigative and feature stories.

The personnel changes come as CBS and other broadcast networks face ongoing challenges in the news division landscape. Traditional network news programs have experienced shifting viewership patterns and increased competition from digital and cable news sources.

CBS has not provided detailed public comment on the reasoning behind the specific personnel decisions or the broader direction planned for 60 Minutes under the new leadership structure.

cards.headline: Four performers withdraw from Trump-linked Freedom 250 concert series
cards.teaser: Martina McBride joined The Commodores and Morris Day in pulling out of National Mall concerts after learning of political associations.
cards.body:
Country singer Martina McBride has withdrawn from the Freedom 250 concert series planned for Washington, D.C.'s National Mall, citing misleading information about the event. She joins at least five other musical acts who have dropped out since the lineup was announced.

Morris Day was among the first to back out, calling his participation a "baseless rumor." The concert series, organized by Trump appointee Keith Krach to celebrate America's 250th anniversary, has faced significant backlash from performers who reconsidered their involvement after the announcement.

cards.headline: CBS defends Byron Allen late-night deal, says it will generate $15 million profit
cards.teaser: The network disclosed financial projections for leasing the late-night hour after canceling The Late Show with Stephen Colbert.
cards.body:
CBS has defended its decision to lease its late-night time slot to Byron Allen rather than continue producing a traditional talk show, citing projected profits of $15 million from the arrangement. The network canceled The Late Show with Stephen Colbert and sold the time slot to Allen for his program Comics Unleashed.

Allen's debut at 11:35 p.m. attracted 995,000 viewers, representing a significant decline from Colbert's finale ratings. The move has faced weeks of criticism over ending CBS's long-running late-night program, though Allen secured the deal after 51 years of pursuing the time slot.

cards.headline: HBO documentary on Jacinda Ardern wins top Emmy award
cards.teaser: Prime Minister, a film about the New Zealand leader, took best documentary at the awards ceremony.
cards.body:
Prime Minister, an HBO documentary about New Zealand leader Jacinda Ardern, won the top documentary prize at the Documentary Emmy Awards. The film was directed by Michelle Walshe and Lindsay Utz and explores Ardern's tenure as prime minister.

The documentary previously won the Audience Award for World Cinema Documentary at the 2025 Sundance Film Festival. National Geographic and Netflix were among the leading winners at the Emmy Awards ceremony.

cards.headline: Maddox Jolie-Pitt files to drop Pitt surname
cards.teaser: The eldest son of Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt filed legal documents to remove his father's last name.
cards.body:
Maddox Jolie-Pitt filed legal documents to drop Pitt from his surname. The move comes amid an ongoing family divide between Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt.

Brad Pitt had no contact with daughter Zahara before her recent college graduation, according to reports. Zahara graduated and also dropped the Pitt surname. Son Pax Thien attended the graduation with other family members.

cards.headline: Richard Gadd discusses Half Man finale and character death
cards.teaser: The creator and star explained the ending of his HBO drama, including a major character's death and a fight sequence.
cards.body:
Richard Gadd opened up about the conclusion of his HBO and BBC drama series "Half Man," which wrapped its six-week run with significant revelations about his character Ruben's relationship with Jamie Bell's Niall.

The finale featured the death of a major character, which Gadd felt provided the appropriate ending for the show. He also reflected on an intense fight scene and the deliberately ambiguous nature of the finale's conclusion. The complete series is now available to stream on HBO Max.

cards.headline: Hacks creators discuss series finale and character endings
cards.teaser: The showrunners and stars reflected on the final episode of the HBO Max comedy, including a twist ending.
cards.body:
The creators and stars of Hacks discussed the series finale of the HBO Max comedy. The final episode featured Deborah Vance and Ava Daniels workshopping jokes together, an activity they had not done for most of the fifth and final season.

The creators said they knew they needed to heighten stakes in the finale but that Deb

hero.headline: US and Iran near agreement to extend ceasefire, reopen Strait of Hormuz
hero.body:
The United States and Iran have reached a tentative agreement to extend their ceasefire by 60 days, reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and establish a framework for talks on Tehran's nuclear program, according to US officials. Vice President JD Vance said on Thursday that the two countries were "very close" to finalizing a memorandum of understanding, though some sticking points remained.

"We're very close but not there yet," Vance said, adding that the US was still "going back and forth" with Iran on nuclear issues.

Negotiators have been working to finalize the terms of the agreement. US officials told the BBC that the framework of a ceasefire extension deal had been agreed, pending approval from President Trump and Iran's leadership. A second round of negotiations would "very likely" be held in Islamabad, according to White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt.

The tentative deal comes after weeks of indirect negotiations, with Pakistan playing a key role in mediation efforts. Pakistan's army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, led a delegation to Tehran on Wednesday to convey messages from Washington. Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also launched a four-day regional tour to Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Turkey to coordinate support for peace efforts.

Leavitt said the White House remained "very much engaged" in negotiations and felt "good about the prospects of a deal." However, she emphasized that nothing was official until announced by the White House.

The proposed agreement would extend the ceasefire beyond its expiration on April 22 and launch further diplomatic efforts. The memorandum would create a framework for broader talks on Tehran's nuclear program and address concerns about Iran's nuclear capabilities. The Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global oil shipments, would reopen under the terms being discussed.

News of the potential breakthrough led to falling oil prices on Thursday, reflecting market optimism about the deal.

However, complications remain on the ground. Sources in Tehran indicated that Iran demanded an end to Israeli attacks on Lebanon as a precondition for another round of negotiations with the US. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu signaled that Israel was continuing military operations against Hezbollah in Lebanon, indicating a potential obstacle to broader regional peace.

The US military has also imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports following earlier negotiations. US warships turned back nine ships, including a Chinese-owned tanker, attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday.

Trump and his advisers have previously believed they were close to a deal several times during negotiations, only to see talks stall. The signing of the memorandum of understanding would represent the most significant diplomatic breakthrough since the war began.

cards.headline: Police respond to swatting call at Justice Amy Coney Barrett's home
cards.teaser: Supreme Court Justice Amy Coney Barrett was targeted in a swatting incident at her Virginia home.
cards.body:
Supreme Court Justice Amy Coney Barrett was the victim of a swatting call at her Virginia home. Police radio traffic shows law enforcement received a call for a suspicious noise of gunshots at Barrett's suburban Virginia address.

The dispatcher warned responding officers shortly afterward that a high priority resident of the county lived there and that the report may not be authentic. Local police responded to the call.

cards.headline: White House launches website highlighting immigrant arrests
cards.teaser: The White House launched a space-themed website that displays arrests of immigrants unauthorized to live in the U.S.
cards.body:
The White House launched a website that touts the arrests of immigrants unauthorized to live in the U.S. The website, launched on Thursday, opens with a crawl similar to the one seen in the Star Wars franchise, with blocks of text.

The site mocks the idea of the U.S. retaining secrets involving alien encounters. The website uses a space theme to present information about immigration enforcement actions.

cards.headline: Pro-Israel groups spend nearly $8 million to defeat Rep. Thomas Massie
cards.teaser: Pro-Israel organizations spent heavily to oust Kentucky Rep. Thomas Massie in what became the most expensive House primary in American history.
cards.body:
Pro-Israel groups spent nearly $8 million to oust GOP Rep. Thomas Massie in Kentucky's 4th District, helping to fuel the most expensive House primary in American history. AI companies, the cryptocurrency industry, and pro-Israel groups are spending at unprecedented levels to defeat their least favorite members of Congress and congressional candidates.

Crypto-aligned Protect Progress was by far the largest spender in some races. The volume of spending is the kind that can kill careers and stop political movements in their tracks.

cards.headline: Martina McBride pulls out of America 250 concert
cards.teaser: Country singer Martina McBride said she will not perform at a National Mall concert celebrating America's 250th birthday, claiming she was misled.
cards.body:
Country singer Martina McBride announced Thursday that she will not perform at a concert series on the National Mall celebrating America's 250th anniversary, organized by the Trump administration. McBride said she was misled about the event's nature, having been told it would be nonpartisan.

Her withdrawal is among at least six musical acts that have dropped out of the concert series in the day following its announcement. Morris Day was the first to exit, calling his participation a baseless rumor.

cards.headline: Michigan Gov. Whitmer walks back comment on 2028 presidential run
cards.teaser: Gov. Gretchen Whitmer reversed course on earlier statements about whether she would run for president in 2028.
cards.body:
Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer walked back a comment saying she would not run for president in 2028. Whitmer, term-limited after two gubernatorial wins in her battleground state, has been widely viewed as a potential Democratic candidate.

The governor's reversal marks a shift in her public stance on future political ambitions. Whitmer won two gubernatorial elections in Michigan, a key battleground state.

cards.headline: Sen. Susan Collins fires back at Iraq war criticism from challenger
cards.teaser: Sen. Susan Collins responded to her Democratic challenger's criticism of her vote supporting the Iraq war.
cards.body:
Sen. Susan Collins responded Thursday to criticism from her Democratic challenger about her voting record on military intervention. Graham Platner, a Marine veteran and oyster farmer running against the incumbent senator, had said Collins voted to send him to Iraq. 

Collins countered that Platner was not drafted, implying his military service was voluntary. The exchange highlights a key point of contention in Maine's competitive Senate race as the election approaches.
